title: Protocol to Study Secretome Interactions Using Extracellular Proximity Labeling
author: Rich, Gurung, et al.
materials: The following analysis assumes Proteome Discoverer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) is the proteomics tool utilized to analyze mass spectra, specifically utilizing the calculated protein peptide spectrum matches (PSMs) and/or abundance between control and treatment samples. Other analysis tools can be utilized, such as the freely available MaxQuant software. Analysis of unlabeled and TMT-labeling experiments is unique.Optional: Final protein candidates can be filtered against the Contaminant Repository for Affinity Purification (CRAPome).9 We utilized an arbitrary candidate exclusion threshold that removes any candidate that is detected in over 99 (out of 716) control experiments within the CRAPome database.

steps.title: Prepare confluent cell dishes
steps.instruction: Ensure each cell line has a confluent 150 mm tissue‑culture dish. Wash cells three times with DPBS, detach with 1000 µL trypsin/EDTA, and resuspend in 10 mL BDFM for counting.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 10 mL BDFM for counting.

steps.title: Seed Media Transfer Cells
steps.instruction: Seed 1.5 × 10⁶ transgene‑expressing cells into a single 150 mm plate (Media Transfer Cells, MTCs).

steps.title: Seed Receiver and WT MTC cells
steps.instruction: Seed 1.5 × 10⁶ wild‑type (WT) cells into five 150 mm plates (four Receiver Cells, RCs, and one WT MTC), adding 25 mL BDFM to each plate. Required cell types per experiment: WT control MTC, biotin‑ligase control MTC, target‑biotin‑ligase MTC, biotin‑ligase‑target MTC, and four WT RCs. (WT control MTC and one WT RC may be omitted if using TMT labeling.)

substeps.instruction: Seed WT cells into 5 × 150 mm plates (4 RCs + 1 WT MTC).
Record which control and experimental cell types are included.

steps.title: Incubate cells three days
steps.instruction: Incubate all plates for 3 days at 5 % CO₂ and 37 °C.

steps.title: Refresh media on Receiver Cells
steps.instruction: Replace 10 mL of media on each RC with fresh BDFM to maintain healthy conditions.

steps.title: Serum‑starve Media Transfer Cells
steps.instruction: Replace the media on the MTCs with 23 mL LSBDM and incubate for 24 h at 5 % CO₂ and 37 °C to achieve serum starvation.

steps.title: Transfer conditioned media
steps.instruction: After the 24 h serum‑starvation, aspirate all media from the RCs and immediately add the conditioned media (≈22 mL after evaporative loss) collected from the MTCs to the RCs.

steps.title: Initiate extracellular proximity labeling
steps.instruction: Add ATP and biotin to the RC media to reach the required working concentrations: for TurboID, 0.1 mM ATP; for BioID2, 2 mM ATP; for both enzymes, 1 µM biotin.

steps.title: Dry and resuspend samples for LC‑MS/MS
steps.instruction: Vacuum‑concentrate each sample to dryness, then resuspend in 16 µL 0.1 % formic acid; use 12 µL of this solution for LC‑MS/MS analysis.

steps.title: LC‑MS/MS analysis (unlabeled)
steps.instruction: Load samples onto a peptide trap cartridge at 5 µL/min, elute onto an Easy‑Spray PepMap RSLC C18 column (2 µm, 100 Å, 75 µm × 250 mm) using a linear acetonitrile gradient (3–36 % in 0.1 % formic acid) over 110 min at 0.3 µL/min. Ionize with a Nano Easy‑Spray source set to 1.6 kV spray voltage and 275 °C capillary temperature. Search unlabeled data against human protein sequences with static carbamidomethylation (+57.021 Da, C), dynamic oxidation/hydroxylation (+15.995 Da, M/P/K) and deamidation (+0.984 Da, N/Q), minimum peptide length 5, precursor tolerance 15 ppm, fragment tolerance 0.05 Da, and FDR ≤ 0.01.

steps.title: LC‑MS/MS analysis (TMT‑labeled)
steps.instruction: Run the instrument in DDA mode: survey MS 350–1800 m/z at 35,000 resolution (200 m/z) with AGC target 3 × 10⁶ and max injection 100 ms; select top 20 multiply‑charged ions (z ≥ 2) for HCD fragmentation (NCE 30) with AGC target 1 × 10⁵, max injection 400 ms, resolution 17,500, isolation window 2 m/z, first mass 120 m/z, dynamic exclusion 30 s, charge‑state screening rejecting unassigned, 1+, 7+, >7+ ions. Search with static carbamidomethylation (+57.021 Da, C) and TMT (+229.163 Da, N‑terminus/K), dynamic oxidation/hydroxylation (+15.995 Da, M/P/K) and deamidation (+0.984 Da, N/Q), minimum peptide length 5, precursor tolerance 15 ppm, fragment tolerance 0.05 Da, FDR ≤ 0.01.

steps.title: Process data and filter candidates
steps.instruction: Analyze raw files with Proteome Discoverer (or MaxQuant), calculate peptide‑spectrum matches or quantitative abundances, compare control versus treatment samples, and optionally filter final protein candidates against the CRAPome, removing any protein detected in >99 of 716 control experiments.

description: The following protocol describes the step-by-step procedure for using proximity labeling in vitro to explore the proximal interactome of secreted factors. We utilized this protocol to study the TIMP2 interactome in HT1080 and HS-5 cells in both 2D and 3D cultures, and we have expanded this protocol to numerous other cell lines and targets.1 All biological processes are propagated through molecular interactions that overwhelmingly occur between components of the proteome. In humans, there are at least 18,000 individual protein identities, a number that soars when considering individual proteoforms.2 Interactome studies provide insights into the functions and subcellular localization of target proteins, the findings of which have proven invaluable across basic and translational biomedical research. The relatively recent proliferation of interactome studies using proximity labeling (PL) has provided researchers with a powerful tool for studying proximal protein-protein interactors (prPPIs) in living systems. These methods rely on the presence or expression of a fusion consisting of the target protein linked to a biotin ligase or an engineered ascorbate peroxidase, the results of which produce complimentary findings to those of classical methods such as affinity purification/mass spectrometry (AP/MS) and yeast 2-hybrid (Y2H).3 PL has several key advantages over traditional interactome study methods, including the ability to capture weak/transient interactions, flexibility with reaction kinetics depending on the chosen PL enzyme, and a reliance on the potent biotin-streptavidin interaction. The biotin-streptavidin interaction is a double-edged sword with regards to its role in the power of PL. On one hand, the strong interaction allows for extensive washing to remove contaminants.
